title: Wittmann turns pole into a fourth win at the Nürburgring
dek: Marco Wittmann won from pole for BMW Team RMG, 1.286 seconds clear of Rockenfeller, as four Audis fell out in early collisions and his championship lead grew to 64 points.

chapters.title: A title leader in a black-ribbon weekend
text: The seventh round of the 2014 DTM season, on Sunday 17 August, came two weeks after BMW had filled the top four places at the Red Bull Ring. BMW had won four of the first six races and arrived with Marco Wittmann leading the drivers' standings on 95 points, 39 clear of Mattias Ekström, with Bruno Spengler third on 42. For BMW Team RMG it was also a home weekend, as the team is based not far from the Eifel circuit.

The mood in the BMW camp was subdued. Dieter Lamm, the twin brother of Schnitzer team principal Charly Lamm and a long-serving member of that team, had died the week before, and all eight BMW M4 DTMs ran with black ribbons. Success was also costly in the other sense: Wittmann, Farfus and Spengler had to carry the maximum 10 kilograms of additional performance weight, and the rest of the BMWs were heavier than their Audi and Mercedes rivals.

Spengler was making his 100th DTM start, on the 3.629-kilometre Grand Prix-circuit variant used for a 49-lap race. Audi, meanwhile, was still looking for its first win of 2014. The format asked for one mandatory pit stop, with every driver required to use both the harder prime and the softer option tyre, so strategy would matter as much as raw pace.

chapters.title: Wittmann clear of a train of Audis
text: Rain disrupted both morning practice sessions and the first part of qualifying, with drivers starting Q1 on wet tyres and switching to slicks as the track dried. That cut both ways. Gary Paffett, who had led the early running, ended up last of the Q1 casualties as the circuit improved in the closing minutes and was left 23rd on the grid, while Ekström, second in the championship, was knocked out too and lined up 22nd. Vitaly Petrov, Joey Hand and António Félix da Costa went out alongside them.

At the front Wittmann was in a class of his own despite the maximum success weight. His 1:22.780 in the final shoot-out took pole, with Edoardo Mortara's first lap of 1:22.925 for Abt the best reply, 0.145 seconds away. Mike Rockenfeller was third in the Phoenix Audi and Jamie Green fourth for Rosberg after leaving his run until the very end. Timo Scheider and Miguel Molina made it five Audis behind the BMW, and his Team RMG team-mate Maxime Martin could only manage 12th.

Daniel Juncadella gave Mücke Motorsport the best Mercedes place in seventh, his first appearance in the top-eight shoot-out of the season, with Paul di Resta eighth and Christian Vietoris ninth for HWA. Nico Müller was tenth for Rosberg. Robert Wickens and Augusto Farfus shared the seventh row in 13th and 14th, and Pascal Wehrlein started 18th, with Spengler 16th and Martin Tomczyk 17th.

chapters.title: Rockenfeller jumps Mortara, Ekström is out
text: Wittmann made a perfect start and led out of the first corner, then pulled out a gap of more than two seconds, which kept Rockenfeller outside the reach of his DRS. The race-defining move behind came on the run to Turn 1, where Rockenfeller got ahead of fellow Audi driver Mortara to take second place, leaving Mortara third.

The back of the field was chaotic. Molina and Green touched at the start, damaging the Spaniard's Audi, and Molina was out by lap four. Ekström, running from 22nd, tangled with Timo Glock's BMW at the third corner and parked his damaged Audi after three laps, ending the championship runner-up's day without points. Glock's own race was compromised as well, and he later fell into a series of contacts with Paffett.

chapters.title: Audi's afternoon unravels
text: The next blow to Audi came on lap eight. Wickens tapped Scheider as the cars braked for the first corner, which pushed Scheider into fellow Audi driver Müller. Both Audis were finished, Scheider in the pits and Müller at the side of the track, and Scheider called the move needless. Müller's race ended on lap ten, so Audi had lost four of its eight cars to collisions inside ten laps.

Green and Farfus then clashed, with the Rosberg driver pushing the BMW wide and off the track. Farfus said the contact cost him his race, and the damaged BMW was retired after 35 laps. Further back Glock and Paffett kept touching, which entertained the crowd but did nothing for either of them. Paffett came home 15th and Glock 16th.

chapters.title: Strategy decides the midfield
text: Wittmann's mandatory stop was quick and clean, and he rejoined in front. There was no safety car in the second stint to bunch the field, so the order barely changed. The one lapse was a late-braking moment at the chicane, where gravel on the line had left his tyres dirty and he had to run straight on without gaining time.

The drivers who started on the harder prime tyre had to stop for options, and the best of them was Tomczyk, who started 17th, ran a strong first stint and worked up to eighth. Spengler and Félix da Costa tried the same tactic but finished only 12th and 13th, and Spengler's team admitted a strategy error. Wickens and Wehrlein, who started 13th and 18th, moved into the points on the standard-tyre route and were ninth and tenth.

chapters.title: Rockenfeller closes to 1.286 seconds
text: Wittmann led every lap bar the one on which he stopped, but his tyres faded in the closing stages and Rockenfeller, who had the fresher rubber, began to reel him in. With a couple of laps left the Phoenix Audi was inside the DRS window, but it never found a way to attack and finished 1.286 seconds behind. Wittmann took the flag after 49 laps in 1:09:42.802, his fourth win of the season, and set the fastest lap of the race on lap two with a 1:23.175.

Mortara completed the podium, 12.019 seconds back, with di Resta on his tail for most of the race and only 12.815 seconds behind the winner in fourth. Juncadella was fifth ahead of Vietoris, so Mercedes had a 4-5-6 and five cars in the top ten, even though its team said the circuit did not suit it. Martin was seventh and Tomczyk eighth.

chapters.title: One hand on the trophy
text: The result opened a gap that looked decisive. Wittmann left the Eifel on 120 points, 64 clear of Ekström and Mortara, who were tied on 56, with Rockenfeller on 53 and Spengler on 42. Only 75 points remained across the last three races, and the arithmetic was clear: at the Lausitzring, a fourth place would be enough to clinch the title even if a rival won. Wittmann himself stayed cautious, saying the races still had to be driven.

BMW's reaction was dominated by Dieter Lamm. Wittmann dedicated the win to the man who had introduced him to the BMW Motorsport family, and motorsport director Jens Marquardt did the same on behalf of the whole organisation while asking supporters to hold back on congratulations, since a race could end quickly. Team RMG principal Stefan Reinhold had tears in his eyes at the flag after a home win, and Charly Lamm thanked BMW, the DTM and the fans for their support during a difficult fortnight at Schnitzer.

For Audi the weekend was a mixed one. Rockenfeller and Mortara gave it two podium places, and Mortara's third moved him from 41 to 56 points and level with Ekström in second, but the team was still waiting for its first win of the season. Audi's Dieter Gass said only those two had made use of good grid positions and that losing four of eight cars to collisions hurt. Rockenfeller described it as a good second place and said five more laps might have made the finish more interesting, while Scheider was angry about what Wickens had done to him. Mercedes, meanwhile, took five cars into the top ten and left satisfied, with di Resta fourth the best of them, while Spengler's weekend ended in 12th after what his team called a strategy error.

Rockenfeller, on 53 points, was still mathematically in the fight, but only just. The next race was at the Lausitzring on 14 September, a full month later, and it carried the prospect of a champion being crowned with two rounds to spare.

facts.v: Wittmann's win at the Nürburgring was his fourth of the 2014 season, and with 120 points he led Ekström and Mortara by 64 with 75 left to win.
